transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-05-13
Start: 15:00 PDT
Duration: ~46 minutes
Attendees: Samira Patel (Redwood AE), Ethan Moore (Redwood SE), Grace Lin (VP Product - VeritasLane), Marco Ruiz (Staff ML Engineer), Anita Desai (CTO), Jordan Park (SRE)

Summary:
Quick weekly POC sync focused on cost/unit economics (tokens per dollar), observed caching savings, and batching tradeoffs after last week's config changes. Agreed next actions: pricing update, run deterministic benchmark with/without prefix caching and two quant levels, and schedule infra deep-dive.

Topics:
- tokens/sec per dollar observed on current pilot traffic mix
- prefix/KV cache measured savings vs hit rates
- batching windows and tail latency tradeoffs
- quantization recommendations and quality checks
- integration/VPC peering blockers

Key links referenced:
- Pilot economics sheet: https://redwood.app/sheets/VERITASLAN-PILOT-ECON (shared)
- Benchmark artifacts (logs): https://redwood.app/benchmarks/ff/83421 (placeholder)

Action items (brief):
- See action_items field for owners/due dates

Transcript:
[00:00:00] Samira: hey everyone, thanks for joining, uh quick roll call, we have samira and ethan from redwood, veritaslane team on the line?
[00:00:12] Grace: hey yeah this is grace, hi, joined.
[00:00:15] Marco: marco here.
[00:00:17] Anita: Anita, hi.
[00:00:20] Jordan: Jordan here.
[00:00:24] Samira: awesome, thanks. quick agenda, we wanna run through last week's pilot numbers, caching hits, batching config, and then agree next steps, ok?
[00:00:35] Grace: sounds good, main thing for product is we need the cost per successful completion under 0.002 tokens per what— sorry— under $0.002 per inference ideally, so the tokens/sec per dollar basically.
[00:00:50] Ethan: mm-hmm, yeah we pulled numbers overnight, i'll share a quick summary, but quick call out: we saw caching savings on repeated prompts around ~28% token reduction end-to-end when prefix cache hit rate is ~42%. that's with the model set to redwood-clarity-7B-quant, the q4_8 variant.
[00:01:12] Marco: can i ask, when you say prefix cache, is that KV cache or the prefill prefix? we call both things differently.
[00:01:20] Ethan: good point — sorry, i should say KV-prefetch / prefix cache, it's the key-value cache that keeps token history and reuses common prefixes. sometimes the transcript or notes call it "key v cache" or "keyvee cache", so yeah that's what we measured.
[00:01:35] Grace: ok, and batching? how did batching affect tail latency last run? we saw a few spikes in p95.
[00:01:42] Ethan: on the 8k-second window, we experimented with a max-batch of 32 and three batching profiles, small/medium/agg. p95 increased by about 120ms on average for the high batch config but tokens/sec per dollar improved ~18%. tradeoff as expected — if you need p50 under 300ms you probably want smaller batches.
[00:02:02] Marco: that matches our expectations. our traffic is bursty — a lot of short queries with medium length responses — so maybe burst policy or latency-first routing is needed.
[00:02:11] Anita: also want to double-check security — are the logs in the benchmark link sanitized? we can't have user PHI pop into shared artifacts.
[00:02:19] Samira: yes we scrubbed PHI; the logs are aggregated and trace ids only. we can also provide an on-prem sample package if you prefer.
[00:02:29] Jordan: about VPC peering, we still have a blocker — our infra team needs the exact egress IP list for the dev cluster, can you confirm?
[00:02:37] Ethan: i'll paste the current egress IPs in the notes and follow up with an official network manifest.
[00:02:42] Grace: perfect.

[00:03:00] Ethan: ok diving into numbers: for the 24-hour snapshot yesterday, average tokens per request was 340, average response length 210 tokens, requests/sec ~4.8, effective tokens/sec per GPU was roughly 12k with current batching. unit econ: roughly 0.37 tokens per dollar?? — sorry i meant tokens per cent-dollar, the sheet converts to tokens per dollar: about 32k tokens / $1 for current config, which maps to about $0.0012 per average request.
[00:03:34] Marco: that $0.0012 includes the cache savings?
[00:03:37] Ethan: yes that's after applying measured 28% cache savings from live hit rates. raw without caching was closer to $0.0017.
[00:03:44] Grace: nice, that puts us closer to our target but still marginal. what about quantization options — does int8 degrade quality for prompts we care about?
[00:03:53] Ethan: we ran a small eval on your top-100 prompts: q4_8 had negligible regressions, int8 showed minor hallucination upticks for long-context multi-turn prompts — 2.4% regression on our eval metric, which might be visible in user-facing product. my recommendation is try q4_8 for baseline, and do targeted int8 experiments for low-risk paths.
[00:04:12] Anita: i want the exact eval script, can you share it so our data-science team can run the same checks in staging?
[00:04:18] Samira: yes we will share the eval harness — ethan will upload it to the shared folder after the call.

[00:05:00] Ethan: also, one config tweak that gave outsized wins — enable prefix-level caching with a conservative TTL (30s) and aggressive normalization of prompts; for your traffic patterns that gave the 28% savings. caveat: normalization must be deterministic, we saw some misses where punctuation variations prevented hits.
[00:05:19] Marco: can you give an example of normalization?
[00:05:22] Ethan: strip trailing whitespace, standardize date formats to ISO, collapse repeated filler tokens, and lower-case non-proper nouns. avoid changing content semantics.
[00:05:33] Grace: is there any quality regression risk with that normalization approach?
[00:05:36] Ethan: minimal, it's mostly string-level transformation. we'll include a test harness to measure hit/miss false positives.

[00:06:00] Samira: ok, pricing question from grace — we'll send an updated pilot pricing that factors in observed hit rates and an uplift for dedicated if you opt for reserved capacity.
[00:06:10] Grace: would dedicated capacity change the unit price materially? our finance wants to know break-even for committed monthly spend.
[00:06:16] Samira: yes reserved/dedicated usually reduces per-token cost by ~15-30% depending on commit level. for your projected throughput our model suggests a 22% unit cost reduction at 3-month commit. we'll surface numbers in the spreadsheet.
[00:06:30] Marco: curious — any notes on fallback strategies? if the cache misses spike or capacity throttles, how does Redwood degrade?
[00:06:37] Ethan: good question. we route by policy: latency-first or cost-first. we also have auto-fallback to cheaper model variants — e.g., redwood-clarity-3B when 7B is saturated — and graceful degradation with rate limiting and queued responses. logs will show the fallback markers for each request.
[00:06:55] Grace: do you have SLOs for the fallback like p95 under X?
[00:06:58] Ethan: fallback SLOs depend on variant; the 3B variant p95 is usually within 30-50% of the 7B p95 but cheaper. we'll model it in the next run.

[00:07:30] Jordan: re: networking — i need the list of egress IPs and also the peering guide, until we complete peering we had to NAT a few calls and that added variability to latency.
[00:07:40] Samira: understood. ethan i believe you have the manifest?
[00:07:43] Ethan: yes will drop it. also quick note, NAT can add jitter, so peering is recommended for stable p95 numbers.

[00:08:30] Grace: any blockers on your side for us trying int8 in a limited path?
[00:08:34] Ethan: none from us — we need your acceptance criteria and sample traffic routing rules so we can split traffic and observe regressions.
[00:08:42] Marco: we'll prepare a routing flag in staging.

[00:09:10] Samira: ok let's look at one concrete example from the sheet — request id sample 4212, long multi-turn support case, caching hit was false, why?
[00:09:20] Ethan: looked into that trace — the user appended a session token in the prompt that prevented normalization and cache match. once we normalized session tokens we got the hit. we'll add a rule to redact session tokens before caching.
[00:09:34] Marco: perfect.

[00:10:00] Grace: pricing again — can you show scenario with and without cache at 30%, 45%, and 60% hit rates so finance can model sensitivity?
[00:10:09] Samira: yes in fact the spreadsheet has a sensitivity tab, i'll update with a conservative/expected/optimistic hit rate scenarios.
[00:10:18] Anita: on compliance, we need to confirm data retention for logs for SOC2 audit. what's the retention for request logs in the pilot?
[00:10:26] Ethan: pilot default is 30 days for debug logs, aggregated metrics kept 90 days; for SOC2 we can offer extended retention and audit log export, we'll follow up with the security package.

[00:11:05] Marco: a technical nit — kv cache replication on multi-gpu shards, do you have consistency windows we should be aware of? we saw a couple of misses where requests hit different workers.
[00:11:15] Ethan: the runtime uses eventual consistency for KV propagation across shards with a 50-200ms sync window depending on load. that's why small windows can still miss; to mitigate we pin sessions to the same shard when low-latency routing is required.
[00:11:33] Jordan: pinning sessions will need sticky routing on our side too — we'll coordinate.

[00:12:00] Samira: moving on — recommended experiments this week: 1) deterministic 1k-sample bench with caching on/off, 2) q4_8 vs int8 split test on low-risk flows, 3) batching profile sweep (max-batch 8/16/32) tracking p50/p95 and tokens/$ — ethan, can you own these?
[00:12:18] Ethan: yep i'll run those and put full results in the benchmark folder. i expect results by monday or tuesday next week.
[00:12:25] Grace: great.

[00:13:00] Marco: one more data ask — can you include distribution of sequence lengths in the benchmark so we can see tail response lengths?
[00:13:07] Ethan: yes will include histograms for prompt and response token lengths.

[00:14:00] Samira: any objections to a short canary on dedicated nodes for 24 hours to validate throughput improvements?
[00:14:08] Anita: we'd need an estimate of cost uplift and rollback plan, but we're open to a 24-hour test.
[00:14:15] Samira: i'll model cost and rollback steps, add to the sheet.

[00:15:00] Grace: ok let's recap and confirm owners.
[00:15:04] Samira: recap: samira send updated pilot pricing + sensitivity (due 5/15); ethan run bench + upload logs (due 5/18); marco provide prompts and staging routing flag (due 5/17); jordan confirm network peering egress list (due 5/20); schedule infra deep-dive week of 5/25 (samira to propose times). any additions?
[00:15:30] Marco: none from me.
[00:15:32] Anita: no.

[00:16:00] Grace: quick question — competitor behaviour, do you know if anthropic offers a similar caching layer? we heard something but not sure.
[00:16:08] Ethan: Anthropic publicly focuses on model improvements, not sure about transparent KV cache offering; openai has some caching recommendations in their docs but it's usually customer-managed. we'll add a brief competitor note.

[00:16:40] Samira: ok that's it for the core items. we'll follow up in the sheet and next week same time?
[00:16:48] Grace: yes same time next week works.

[00:17:00] --- end of main meeting transcript snippet (additional Q&A and network specifics continued, total duration ~46m)
